input.quote: 18.1 This Agreement shall become effective on the date and year first above written and shall continue in operation for at least an initial period of twenty-five (25) years following the RFS Date (hereinafter referred to as \"initial Period\") and shall be terminable thereafter by agreement of the Parties. However, any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties.
input.rationale: Clause 18 sets a single 25-year Initial Period running from the RFS Date, after which the Agreement simply continues in operation and is "terminable thereafter by agreement of the Parties" (18.1), with termination during the Initial Period by written agreement of all Parties (18.2) and post-Initial-Period decommissioning by a two-thirds voting-interest agreement (18.3). There is no automatic renewal term, no non-renewal notice window and no renewal price-uplift mechanic anywhere in the document, so every conditional automatic-renewal element (12-month renewal term, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder, CPI/3% or 5% uplift cap) is inapplicable, and continuation past the Initial Period rests on agreement of the Parties rather than a unilateral Vendor-favouring roll-over. The one-year written notice in 18.1 is our own unilateral exit right (exercisable at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter, not a condition on continuation) and therefore benefits us; it is an exit mechanic rather than a non-renewal notice window and is not redlined here. Worth noting for completeness that the structure gives us no fixed renewal-pricing protection because no renewal pricing exists to cap; this is a drafting-note point, not a fallback failure.
